harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Repaired /srv/inventory on node1: created inventorysvc user and inventory-readers group, chowned the tree recursively to inventorysvc:inventory-readers, and set dirs to 750 / files to 640 so the owner has full access, the group can read/traverse, and others have no access. Existing data (records.csv, config.json) was preserved unchanged. Completed the mandatory single-node restart protocol: captured a healthy baseline (boot_id, perms, checksums), rebooted node1 via systemd-run reboot, confirmed the node became briefly unreachable then reachable again with a changed boot_id, and verified permissions/ownership and data checksums were identical post-reboot.
actions_performed: Inspected /srv/inventory current ownership/permissions and confirmed inventorysvc user and inventory-readers group did not yet exist
Created inventory-readers group and inventorysvc system user (nologin)
Recursively chowned /srv/inventory to inventorysvc:inventory-readers
Set directory permissions to 750 and file permissions to 640 across /srv/inventory
Verified permissions/ownership and that file contents (records.csv, config.json) were unchanged
Captured baseline boot_id, permissions, and md5 checksums before restart
Scheduled and executed a reboot of node1 via systemd-run /usr/sbin/reboot
Polled node1 until it became reachable again, observing transient connection timeouts during the reboot window
Confirmed boot_id changed (98aa35f5... -> 295b8b70...), proving an actual restart occurred
Re-verified post-reboot that ownership, permissions, group/user existence, and file checksums were all unchanged

evidence.requirement: Existing /srv/inventory contents owned by inventorysvc, group inventory-readers, inaccessible to others
evidence.summary: Before: all root:root 755/644. After: chown -R to inventorysvc:inventory-readers and chmod to 750 (dirs) / 640 (files), verified via find with mode/user/group, with no permission bits for other users.

records.csv and config.json content displayed intact after chown/chmod, and md5 checksums (f9ba9b1c2df16eae39e065f5446f3db4 and 1e4a8c2546b3a592368a5bbc4efac40a) match before and after the restart, proving no data was altered.

evidence.requirement: Mandatory restart protocol: healthy baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Captured baseline boot_id 98aa35f5-6905-42fd-9f07-0e28f75b4fa6 and inventory health; issued systemd-run reboot which acknowledged before disconnect; observed connection timeouts confirming the node was down; polled until reachable again with new boot_id 295b8b70-5017-4d25-a9d1-a3fe4f0f6725; verified post-reboot permissions, ownership, and checksums all match the pre-restart state.
